title: Local prolongation of a tensor power of a symmetric line
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $p:G\to S$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with identity $e$. The addition, inverse and identity are $S$-morphisms satisfying the commutative group identities; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Assume every geometric fibre is semiabelian: after an algebraically closed residue-field extension $k$, it fits into an exact sequence of fppf sheaves $1\to\mathbf G_{m,k}^r\to G_k\to A_k\to1$, where $r\geq0$, $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$, and $A_k$ is a proper smooth geometrically connected $k$-group scheme. Let $U\subseteq S$ be a dense open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion], and put $G_U=G\times_SU$. A line means an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module]; all module pullbacks are tensor inverse images [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $N$ be a line on $G_U$ with a rigidification $e_U^*N\simeq\mathcal O_U$ and an isomorphism $[-1]^*N\simeq N$ of underlying modules. There is an affine open covering $S=\bigcup_iW_i$ such that for each nonempty $W_i$ there are an integer $d_i\geq1$, a line $P_i$ on $G_{W_i}$, and an isomorphism $P_i|_{G_{U\cap W_i}}\simeq N^{\otimes d_i}|_{G_{U\cap W_i}}$. No rigidification or cubical structure on $P_i$ is asserted. No ampleness hypothesis on $N$ and no ampleness conclusion on $P_i$ is imposed.

source.place: II 3.3.3, opening power-prolongation input (Raynaud, Faisceaux amples, XI 1.13). Agent-formulated local non-positive version. Local originals WANTED; this is only the tensor-power input, not II 3.3 symmetric essential surjectivity.

proof.text: Apply the generic torus-quotient node to $G\to S$ to obtain a torus $T\subseteq G$ and a homomorphism $q:G\to H$ which is a $T$-torsor, where $H$ is a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation with semiabelian (hence connected) geometric fibres and $H_\eta$ is an abelian variety. The affine covering of $S$ is chosen in step 3; everything in steps 1--2 takes place over $S$ or on generic fibres. The generic fibre $q_\eta:G_\eta\to H_\eta$ is a $T_\eta$-torsor, and $H_\eta$ is smooth, separated, of finite type and geometrically integral. Apply rational Picard descent to $N_\eta$ to obtain $c\geq1$ and $M_0$ on $H_\eta$ with $q^*M_0\simeq N_\eta^{\otimes c}$. Put $M=M_0\otimes[-1]^*M_0$. Since $q$ is a homomorphism, $q\circ[-1]=[-1]\circ q$, so $q^*M\simeq N_\eta^{\otimes c}\otimes[-1]^*N_\eta^{\otimes c}\simeq N_\eta^{\otimes 2c}$ by the symmetry of $N$; and $M$ is symmetric.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1.7; Sansuc Proposition 6.10; tensor rearrangement from the cited invertible-pullback lemma.

proof.text: Write $M=A\otimes B^{-1}$ with $A,B$ ample on $H_\eta$ by the ample-difference node ($H_\eta$ is a separated finite-type group over $\kappa(\eta)$). The pullback of an ample line along the automorphism $[-1]$ is ample, so $\Sigma A=A\otimes[-1]^*A$ and $\Sigma B=B\otimes[-1]^*B$ are symmetric ample by the existing ample-tensor node, and $\Sigma M=\Sigma A\otimes(\Sigma B)^{-1}$ by functoriality and reordering of tensor factors. Since $M$ is symmetric, $\Sigma M\simeq M^{\otimes2}$, hence $q^*\Sigma M\simeq N_\eta^{\otimes4c}$.

source.place: Lemmas 0BF7 and 0FVC as recorded by the cited DAG nodes; tensor rearrangement is elementary.

proof.text: $H$ has connected fibres by step 1, so the local-ample node gives an affine open covering $S=\bigcup_iW_i$ and ample lines $R=R_i$ on $H_W$, $W=W_i$ nonempty. Ampleness pulls back along the affine morphism $H_\eta\to H_W$, so $R_\eta$ is ample, and $L=R_\eta\otimes[-1]^*R_\eta$ is symmetric ample. The endomorphism-span node, applied on the abelian variety $H_\eta$, gives $a,b\geq1$ and endomorphisms $u_i,v_j$ of $H_\eta$ with $(\Sigma A)^{\otimes a}\simeq\bigotimes u_i^*L$ and $(\Sigma B)^{\otimes b}\simeq\bigotimes v_j^*L$. Since $H$ has semiabelian geometric fibres, generic homomorphism extension (with $P=Q=H$) extends all $u_i,v_j$ to endomorphisms of $H$, restricted to $H_W$. Set $\Sigma R=R\otimes[-1]^*R$, $E_A=\bigotimes u_i^*\Sigma R$, $E_B=\bigotimes v_j^*\Sigma R$, and $P=q^*(E_A^{\otimes b}\otimes E_B^{-\otimes a})$ on $G_W$. Then $(E_A)_\eta\simeq(\Sigma A)^{\otimes a}$, $(E_B)_\eta\simeq(\Sigma B)^{\otimes b}$, so $P_\eta\simeq q^*(\Sigma A\otimes(\Sigma B)^{-1})^{\otimes ab}=q^*(\Sigma M)^{\otimes ab}\simeq N_\eta^{\otimes 4abc}$.

source.place: VI 2.4 and XI 1.14; Lan Proposition 3.3.1.5; tensor calculation from the displayed isomorphisms.

proof.text: Replace $P$ by $P\otimes p^*(e^*P)^\vee$ and normalize the generic comparison at the identity. This rigidifies $P$ without changing the generic comparison, because $e^*N\simeq\mathcal O$ and $p\circ e=\mathrm{id}$.

On an affine noetherian member $W$ of the base cover, clear denominators in finitely many affine trivializations of $P$, $N$, and the generic comparison and its inverse. After shrinking to a dense open $V\subset U\cap W$, this gives an isomorphism $P|_{G_V}\simeq N^{\otimes d}|_{G_V}$ with $d=4abc$.

source.place: Lemma 0C4S and the affine denominator argument; finite type over noetherian makes the total space noetherian.

proof.text: Every geometric fibre of $G$ is connected: it is a torus torsor over a connected abelian variety, the quotient map is open and surjective with connected fibres, so a clopen decomposition of the source would give one of the target. Hence the vertical Cartier-descent node applies to $G_{U\cap W}\to U\cap W$ with dense open $V$; it gives that $G_{U\cap W}$ is normal integral. Let $s$ be the rational section of $P\otimes(N^{\otimes d})^\vee$ on $G_{U\cap W}$ defined by the comparison. It is an invertible regular section on $G_V$, so its divisor $D$ is supported outside $G_V$. The node gives $D=p^*e^*D$. By step 4 and step 5 the section $e^*s$ is $1$ on $V$ (both are regular sections on the integral scheme $V$ with the same generic value), hence $e^*s$ is the constant rational section $1$ and $e^*D=0$. Therefore $D=0$, and the node says $s$ is everywhere invertible on $G_{U\cap W}$, which supplies the required isomorphism. The affine $W_i$ cover $S$, with $P_i=P$ and $d_i=4abc\geq1$ on each.

source.place: II 3.3.3 comparison by a vertical divisor; the cited node is the precise divisor statement.

lean.statement: theorem symmetricLinePowerProlongation {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral S] [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (hS : ∀ s : S, IsDomain (S.presheaf.stalk s) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (G : Grp (Over S)) [IsCommMonObj G.X] [Smooth G.X.hom] [IsSeparated G.X.hom] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.X.hom] [QuasiCompact G.X.hom] (hG : HasSemiabelianGeometricFibres G) (U : S.Opens) (hU : Dense (U : Set S)) (N : ((Over.pullback U.ι).mapGrp.obj G).X.left.Modules) [N.IsInvertible] (rigidification : (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback η[((Over.pullback U.ι).mapGrp.obj G).X].left).obj N ≅ 𝟙_ U.toScheme.Modules) (symmetry : (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback ι[((Over.pullback U.ι).mapGrp.obj G).X].left).obj N ≅ N) : ∃ (I : Type u) (W : I → S.Opens), (⨆ i, W i) = ⊤ ∧ (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (W i)) ∧ ∀ i, Nonempty (W i) → ∃ (d : ℕ), 1 ≤ d ∧ ∃ (P : (pullback G.X.hom (W i).ι).Modules), P.IsInvertible ∧ Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.fst (pullback.fst G.X.hom (W i).ι) (pullback.fst G.X.hom U.ι))).obj P ≅ (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.snd (pullback.fst G.X.hom (W i).ι) (pullback.fst G.X.hom U.ι))).obj (N.tensorPow d))
